answer:
Focus on self-serve startups for the next 90 days, with this year’s roadmap directed toward that segment. Thirty paying customers, one-day integration and growing revenue provide stronger evidence of repeatable demand than two enterprise prospects.

You currently generate $6,300 monthly. If $45,000 is net cash burn, runway is approximately 14.2 months; if it means total monthly expenses, flat revenue extends runway to approximately 16.5 months. Confirm that distinction immediately.

Enterprise procurement would consume six to seven months before payment, potentially longer with implementation and payment terms. One contract contributes only $7,500 monthly; both contribute $15,000 before added costs. SOC 2, on-premises deployment and ongoing support also create obligations beyond the initial build. Neither prospect currently justifies committing your entire roadmap.

At sustained 15% monthly growth, self-serve revenue reaches approximately $34,000 monthly in twelve months. That is promising, but four months of growth does not establish durability, and revenue is not gross profit. Model slower growth, churn and rising processing costs before assuming you can reach profitability.

Keep usage-based pricing so revenue expands with customers. Test a 20–30% higher rate for new customers while preserving easy entry. Judge it by conversion, retention and gross profit per signup; $210 average spend alone does not prove underpricing. Offer prepaid usage commitments where customers want them.

Prioritize improvements through customer interviews and observed bottlenecks. Review activation, cohort retention, expansion and contribution margins after 90 days. Cut spending or begin fundraising preparation early enough to preserve nine months of runway.

Reconsider enterprise only with binding commitments, upfront funding, reusable requirements and pricing that covers implementation, support and displaced self-serve growth.
